Observation: Base plate secured by protruding screws at four non-loadbearing locations
Explanation: The equipment board plate (base plate) has been secured to the cabin floor using protruding screws at four locations. The attachment points do not appear to correspond to designated load-bearing members, frames or stringers. Evidence of local deformation/strain is reportedly visible on the aircraft skin/frame structure beneath the cabin floor.
QA Concern:
The floor board should not be assumed to be a suitably primary structural load path without substantiation. Fasteners installed at non-approved locations can introduce concentrated loads into the floor/skin/frame system.

The reported deformation is a significant structural QA finding and should not be treated as surface level irregularity.

Observation: Runner mat/interposing material between equipment base plate and aircraft floor
Explanation: A runner mat/interposing material has been provided between the equipment mounting base plate and the aircraft floor/floor structure
QA Concern: If the runner mat is electricity insulating, it may interrupt the intended equipment-to-aircraft bonding/ground path and increase the risk of static charge accumulation, electromagnetic interference or ineffective fault-current return.

Observation: No torque value specified in DML
Explanation: The DML does not specify the required torque values for the equipment/base-plate attachment fasteners.
QA Concern: Torque cannot safely be selected merely from the screw diameter. Correct torque depends upon fastener material/grade, thread condition, lubrication, locking method, joint materials and engineering design in line with aviation standards.

Observation: Loose cable secured together with a hydraulic line
Explanation: During cable routing, the electrical cable has been secured/tied together with an existing hydraulic line.
QA Concern: The hydraulic line may be subject to movement, pressure pulsation and vibration different from that of the electrical cable. Direct attachment can result in cable chafing, insulation damage, connector loading or transmission of vibration to the cable.

Observation: Cable routing in cabin differs from approved DML
Explanation: The installed cable routing in cabin was found to differ slightly from the routing depicted in the approved Draft Modification Leaflet (DML).
QA Concern: Even a seemingly minor deviation can alter bend radius, support, spacing and chafing protection or accessibility.

Observation: Ad-hoc cable route from underside of aircraft to cockpit control panel
Explanation: The cable from the underside of the aircraft to the cockpit control panel has been routed as an apparent ad-hoc arrangement following the existing control panel of RMI. Although the removed system is presently not in use, the newly installed cable route does not appear to be fully defined/substantiated in the approved DML.
QA Concern: An undocumented route underneath the aircraft may expose the cable to contaminants, mechanical impact, vibration and inadequate support. The removal of a previously installed panel does not automatically establish the suitability of its former cable route for a new system.

Observation: Inadequate bonding of equipment/system to aircraft
Explanation: The bonding arrangement of the installed system to the aircraft was not found to be adequate. The sub systems are bonded at a common bonding point on the equipment base plate. However, no effective bonding path was observed between the equipment base plate and the aircraft. Further, the rubber mat provided between the base plate and aircraft floor appears to interrupt the bonding path between the equipment and aircraft.
QA Concern: A common bonding point between sub equipment does not by itself establish an adequate bond between the complete system and the aircraft. The insulating mat between the base plate and aircraft floor may result in an open or high resistance bonding path unless a separate approved bonding jumper/ground connection is provided.

Observation: Battery and other consumables – aviation qualification
Explanation: The aviation qualification/acceptance status of the battery and other consumables incorporated in the modification should be established from objective documentary evidence. COTs should not be accepted solely on the basis of electrical rating or physical compatibility.
QA Concern: Usage of an inadequately qualified/non-aviation standard battery/consumable can result in overheating, leakage, fire, reduced capacity or failure under aircraft vibrations/environmental conditions.

Observation: Qualification and aviation experience of technical crew
Explanation: Personnel involved in installation/modification activities reportedly have limited or no aviation background and limited exposure to aircraft-specific standards.
QA Concern: Lack of aviation specific competency can result in incorrect cable routing, improper termination, inappropriate fasteners, incorrect torque application, inadequate bonding, structural damage, FOD and non-compliance with approved modification data.
